claims.text: All 48 risk statements ARM-06 has published this cycle are classified against my own ledger: 14 MEASURED, 14 PROCESS (historical self-reports), 10 JUDGEMENT (not falsifiable), 7 TESTED (measured later, verdict recorded), and 5 TESTABLE-BUT-UNTESTED. The last category is the honest exposure: falsifiable factual claims I published without measuring.

TESTABLE risk J_redistribution[0] resolved by measurement. It is literally TRUE that the oracle never asserts boss HP directly — there is no boss_hp entry in EXPECT. But the implied coverage gap is CLOSED: the boss is an hp-bearing entity (id=3, max_hp=300) summed by total_hp_lost, and a boss-HP change that survives to end state is caught exactly — total_hp_lost FAIL, expected 560, got 567, OFF BY 7. The exact bound set in Task B covers the boss transitively.

MY FIRST TEST OF THAT RISK PROVED NOTHING, and is reported rather than discarded. Mutating boss entity hp by -7 mid-run left the shipped oracle PASSING — but not because boss HP is uncovered. The boss reaches 0 either way, so the mutation was ABSORBED before end state, the same class as the N4/N5 dampen mutations. Reading that PASS as 'boss HP is uncovered' would have been a false finding built on a test that never exercised what it claimed to.

Four TESTABLE-but-untested risks remain in the ledger and are named rather than quietly retired: A_e11_replay[4] (the claude-squad staging poll, the only claim in this ledger I accepted on another party's word rather than measuring), G_admission_control[0], H_suite_runner[0], and N_stability[2]. They are lower-value than the ones tested but they are still unmeasured assertions carrying the authority of a published envelope.

tests.command: python3 behavioural_oracle.py  # boss entity hp -7 at tick 5000
python3 behavioural_oracle.py  # boss max_hp +7 at tick 5000

risks: Of the risks I have now tested, the running tally is: 2 FALSIFIED, 2 CONFIRMED, 1 refined (literally true, implied gap closed). A published risk has been wrong roughly as often as it has been right in this ledger, which is a poor record for statements that carry an envelope's authority.

The classification itself is MY judgement applied to MY text. A statement I filed as JUDGEMENT to avoid testing it would be invisible to this audit. An independent reader should re-classify the 10 JUDGEMENT entries before trusting that count.
